subject: Production incident: inference error surge and timeouts
messages:
From: Maria Santos <maria.santos@brightpath.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@brightpath.ai
Date: 2027-03-02T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Production: surge of 5xx/429 on inference calls

Karthik,

We started seeing a major spike in 5xx and 429 responses from the Redwood hosted inference endpoint for our production traffic around 08:50 PDT. Customers are experiencing transaction failures and degraded UX — checkout flows are timing out and retries are amplifying the problem.

Symptoms:
- ~40% of requests are returning 5xx (500/503) or 429 over the past 20 minutes
- Median latency rising from ~120ms to ~1.8s; tail >10s
- Errors correlate with peaks in traffic but are sustained beyond short bursts
- A sample request-id: req-7f3a2b (attached screenshot of console logs)

We need urgent help. Please advise on next steps and whether you can move us to a different pool or route to a dedicated endpoint while you investigate. Our SREs are standing by.

Attached: incident-screenshot.png

Thanks,
Maria Santos
Head of Platform Reliability
BrightPath AI
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-02T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: surge of 5xx/429 on inference calls

Team —

Forwarding BrightPath's report. They're seeing sustained 5xx/429 and latency spikes. Customer impact is high (checkout failures). Immediate asks:

1) Rachel — can you triage the hosted pool autoscaler and check GPU utilization/queue backlog? Look for autoscale cooldowns or failed scale events.
2) Evelyn — any chance to temporarily route BrightPath traffic to their Dedicated pool or spin up an isolated capacity slice? If not, can we create an emergency routing rule to favor lower-loaded regions?
3) Marissa/Neha — please acknowledge the customer and communicate a short mitigation plan and ETA; keep them in tight loop.
4) All — consider whether client-side retry behavior is amplifying (thundering retries). If so, short-term mitigations (advice to reduce concurrency or increase backoff) may help.

I'm standing by on this thread; if needed we'll escalate to execs.

-Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-02T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: surge of 5xx/429 on inference calls

Quick triage notes (observed 09:00–10:00 PDT):

- Metrics: hosted-pool-us-west-2
  - GPU utilization: peaked at 98% across the pool between 08:45–09:10
  - Pending queue depth: sustained high queue (avg 3.6x normal)
  - Autoscaler: multiple scale-up attempts, but new instances failed to register with runtime due to a kernel panic on the latest AMI in 2 nodes (see logs).
  - Result: transient capacity exhaustion -> increased 5xx (503) followed by 429 when throttling enacted.

- Retry amplification: many client retries with short backoff caused a repeat spike in queue depth. We observed identical request-ids repeated from same IP ranges.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Applied emergency throttling rule for BrightPath logical route (rate-limited to reduce retry amplification).
- Rebalanced some customers to secondary hosted pool (us-east) to free capacity.
- Disabled automatic scaling on affected AMI pool and forced ASG to use last-known-good AMI for new nodes.

Suggested short-term actions (next 2–6 hours):
1) Route BrightPath traffic to their Dedicated endpoint (if they accept) or provide a pre-warmed slice while we validate AMI.
2) Customer-side: recommend increasing retry backoff (exponential, >=1s) and lowering concurrency for 30 minutes.
3) Ops: rollback faulty AMI across affected nodes; run health checks; increase scale-up aggressiveness temporarily (shorter cooldown).

I've attached autoscale-metrics.csv with timeline and node error extracts. Will follow up with a postmortem stub.

-Rachel
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Santos <maria.santos@brightpath.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-02T11:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: surge of 5xx/429 on inference calls

Maria — thanks for the flag and the logs. Apologies for the disruption. We have a small mitigation plan that can be actioned immediately:

1) Option A (fast): We can route your traffic to a pre-warmed dedicated slice for the next 4 hours. This will reduce your error rate while we fix the underlying AMI issue. Link to provisioning request: https://console.redwood.ai/dedicated/provision?acct=brightpath
2) Option B (if you prefer): Follow SRE guidance to increase retry backoff and drop concurrency; we'll rate-limit at the edge to avoid retry amplification.

If you approve Option A, we'll request provisioning and confirm ETA (~18–30 minutes). As a gesture for the outage, we will credit one day of metered usage to your account.

Attached: maintenance_plan.pdf (short timeline & steps).

Will stand by for your preference.

-Marissa
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-02T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: surge of 5xx/429 on inference calls — exec note

Thanks for the quick work getting metrics and mitigations in place. A few executive actions:

- Approve the one-day credit for BrightPath and offer a 10% bill credit if we see more than one additional incident in the next 30 days (Marissa, please draft the escalation/offering language).
- Incident postmortem: engineering to produce a timeline and root cause (AMI regression + autoscale cooldown) within 48 hours. Include steps to prevent repeat (pre-warm policy changes, canary AMI rollout, autoscaler tuning).
- Ops: prioritize rollback of the faulty AMI and a small automation change to detect node registration failures earlier (health-check alert threshold).
- Customer comms: provide BrightPath with the dedicated-slice option immediately and a short customer-oriented one-page executive summary once postmortem is ready.

I'll brief GTM & legal as needed. Keep me posted; if BrightPath escalates externally, route PR/comms to me directly.

-Sean
VP, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
